label: Transcoded
headline: Lossy audio in an Example wrapper
sub: The spectrum stops dead at 16.1 kHz, the signature of 128 kbps MP3/AAC, later upsampled to 96 kHz. Converting to lossless can’t restore what the encoder removed.

findings.title: Brick-wall cutoff at 16.1 kHz
findings.detail: A lossless 96 kHz file can carry content up to 48.0 kHz. Here it drops 62 dB within about a kilohertz at 16.1 kHz, which is what a lossy encoder’s lowpass filter leaves behind. Most likely source: 128 kbps AAC or MP3, the classic cutoff of YouTube’s AAC stream (format 140), SoundCloud MP3s and older Fraunhofer encoders.

findings.title: Only 16 of 24 bits used
findings.detail: The lowest 8 bits are zero in every sample: this is 16-bit audio padded out to 24 bits. The padding carries nothing.
